input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.
input.rationale: Despite the one-sided heading ("Limitation of Garman's Liability"), Section 15 operates mutually: the direct-damages remedy and the exclusion of special, indirect and consequential damages both apply to "either party", and the final sentence disapplies the limitation for breaches of Sections 13 (intellectual property) and 14 (confidentiality) — our two principal exposure areas sit outside it. Critically, there is no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement (no aggregate/cap/exceed language appears on search), so Garman's liability for direct damages is uncapped. That is better for us than the preferred position of a cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, and none of the walk-away triggers apply: there is no one-way cap protecting only the Vendor and no language capping Garman while leaving us unlimited. Our own direct-damages exposure is equally uncapped, but introducing the playbook cap would principally benefit Garman by limiting our recovery, so we do not redline. Sub-elements short of preferred, noted only: the carve-outs do not expressly name gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and there is no statement that our payment obligations are not "damages" for these purposes.
